tldr: DeepSeek's retrained V4-Flash beat flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks in late July, released amid an intensifying China AI price war, before going fully open-source. A week of price-hike warnings led into V4 Pro's confirmed Aug 13 launch at sharply higher prices alongside Harness, DeepSeek's open-source answer to Claude Code.
whats_new: DeepSeek's Aug 24 second multimodal model is still single-sourced 24+ hours later — no second outlet has named the model or published a benchmark, and it remains unclear whether it's distinct from Aug 21's V4-Flash-Vision-Exp.
why_it_matters: Treat the Aug 24 release as unconfirmed until a second source corroborates it — a full day on, none has. For cost planning, the operative signal is still Aug 23's partial pricing rollback: the weekend surcharge is gone, but the underlying V4 Pro hike stands.

status.state: Weekend peak-pricing surcharge dropped, but the underlying V4 Pro hike still stands
status.detail: Harness open-sourced alongside V4 Pro's Aug 13 launch, then reached China's state supercomputing network Aug 15. V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (Aug 21) claims to come close to Opus 4.8 on agent benchmarks. DeepSeek ended the weekend surcharge Aug 23, even as cumulative prices stay up 355% since the hike. A single outlet's Aug 24 second-model report remains unconfirmed a day later.

beats.headline: Price-hike reports build for over a week, and an early hands-on already finds cracks in the "cheaper" pitch
beats.summary: Bloomberg, Investing.com, TechNode, The Next Web, China Daily, Semafor, Mashable, a CITIC note, and regional coverage flag a coming price increase for a week and a half before V4 Pro's launch makes it real. The-decoder.com's Aug 12 check still finds DeepSeek beating MAI Code on price and performance; The New Stack's Aug 10 hands-on finds the "better and cheaper" promise holds only partly.

beats.headline: DeepSeek publicizes a dedicated team building agent tools to rival Claude Code
beats.summary: A Pi-founder claim that DeepSeek plus Pi already beats Claude Code opens the day; hours later Bloomberg is first to report DeepSeek forming a team aimed squarely at Anthropic's Claude Code, corroborated same-day by PYMNTS' "new team" framing and repeated by briefs.co and TradingView into Aug 13 — hours before that team's tool ships.

beats.headline: A wave of Qwen 3.8 coverage rides the same open-weight keyword cluster
beats.summary: Not part of the DeepSeek story: ten Qwen 3.8 pieces — release, hardware runs, and comparisons vs. Kimi K3/GPT-5.6/Claude Opus — swept in by the shared "open weight" search cluster. Flagged for transparency, not narrative continuity.

beats.headline: A quiet OpenRouter build becomes DeepSeek's officially confirmed V4 Pro release, at sharply higher prices
beats.summary: Simon Willison spots the refreshed Pro model listed API-only with no announcement page; a day later, Lufkin Daily News, Reuters, The Information, and Global Times confirm it as a deliberate release at sharply higher user prices, with The Information framing it as a direct challenge to Kimi K3.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Harness, a free Claude Code rival, and puts it on China's state supercomputing network
beats.summary: VentureBeat reports the free, open-sourced Harness tool shipping alongside pricier V4-Pro; DeepSeek frames V4 Pro's exit from preview around agent-capability gains without publishing benchmarks. CGTN and Analytics India Magazine repeat the framing; two days later Global Times reports both live on China's National Supercomputing Internet, a channel beyond the commercial API.

beats.headline: Recap widens to a US-China AI-race frame, quantifies the hike, then pits V4 Pro's price and capability against Qwen 3.8 Max
beats.summary: Coverage widens: benchmark gains cited, the hike framed as a strategy shift and a US-China race, Forbes quantifies it at 14x the cheapest model, and TheSequence reviews it alongside GLM-5.3 and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Willison's Artificial Analysis check puts Qwen 3.8 27B one point behind V4 Pro — DeepSeek's open-weight edge is thin. Memeburn reframes the hike against Qwen 3.8 Max.

beats.headline: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, its first multimodal model pitched against Opus 4.8
beats.summary: Eight outlets corroborate the vision-capable model over two days — Seeking Alpha and Investing.com first, then Cryptonews ties it to reported IPO speculation, oodaloop and the-decoder frame it against Opus 4.8's agent-benchmark performance, and Tech in Asia confirms the vision-capable test build a day later with no new capability claims.

beats.headline: DeepSeek drops its weekend peak-pricing surcharge, even as cumulative peak prices remain up sharply
beats.summary: Bloomberg and a second outlet report DeepSeek ending the weekend peak-pricing surcharge for API users the same day a comparison piece puts cumulative peak-price increases at 355% since the original hike — an incremental de-escalation, not a reversal of the underlying V4 Pro price increase.

beats.headline: DeepSeek ships a second multimodal model Aug 24 — still single-source, no name or benchmark 24+ hours later
beats.summary: TahawulTech.com remains the only outlet reporting it. No second source has named the model or clarified whether it's distinct from the Aug 21 V4-Flash-Vision-Exp launch.

open_questions: Is the Aug 24 "new multimodal model" a distinct release from V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, or delayed/duplicate coverage of the same Aug 21 launch — what's the model's actual name and spec?
Does V4 Pro's claimed "agent gains" reclaim the benchmark lead V4-Flash took in July, or does Flash remain the stronger agent option?
Forbes prices V4 Pro at 14x DeepSeek's cheapest model — is that still cheaper than Qwen 3.8 Max per token, or has DeepSeek lost its price edge to Alibaba?
Does V4-Flash-Vision-Exp's "comes close to Opus 4.8" claim rest on a published benchmark, or is it qualitative positioning?
Does ending the weekend peak-pricing surcharge signal a broader course-correction on pricing, or is it a narrow carve-out that leaves the underlying V4 Pro hike intact?
take_for_builders: Hold off updating any DeepSeek multimodal comparison until a second outlet names the Aug 24 model and its benchmarks — none has in the 24+ hours since. Separately, re-check current weekend/off-peak API rates before locking a cost model: pricing has moved twice since the August hike.
